interludes.speaker: cook
interludes.text: Chef Marco found the extra food crates from the cargo hold. Throw a feast, or save them?
interludes.fact: Food is heavy to launch, so Mars planners want meals that are light, tasty and last for years.

interludes.speaker: eng
interludes.text: The water recycler is wheezing again. A spare pump from the cargo hold could fix it for good.
interludes.fact: Real Mars plans include spare parts and 3D printers, because the nearest repair shop is tens of millions of kilometers away.

interludes.speaker: sci
interludes.text: Layered clay rocks sit in the old river delta. They might hold signs of ancient life. Collect some?
interludes.fact: Perseverance is collecting rock samples at Jezero's delta for a future mission to bring them to Earth.

interludes.speaker: ops
interludes.text: Wind keeps coating our panels with dust on these open plains. Clean them now, or wait for a gust?
interludes.fact: On Mars, wind sometimes cleans solar panels. In 2005, 'dust devils' cleaned Spirit rover's panels and boosted its power.

interludes.speaker: eng
interludes.text: The old damage from our rough trip is creaking. A hairline crack is leaking air slowly.
interludes.fact: Mars habitats must hold air against a thin atmosphere pressing from outside. Even tiny cracks matter.

interludes.speaker: med
interludes.text: Thanks to the cruise workouts, the crew can haul heavy rocks. Build a wall around the habitat?
interludes.fact: Mars gravity is only 38% of Earth's. Staying strong from exercise keeps bones healthy for the trip home.
